title: Schedule of Verification Deadlines, Extensions and Late Completion — Claimant Identity Verification
content:
The time limits of Claimant Identity Verification are fixed per proofing pathway. All day counts in Schedule A are calendar days; the mail review period in Schedule B is counted in business days.

## Schedule A — Deadline, extensions and late completion (calendar days)

| Pathway | Deadline: days after the notice date | Days added by one extension | Extensions allowed per case | Late completion window after the deadline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Online Identity Proofing (IAL2) | 21 | 14 | 1 | 30 |
| Video Trusted Referee Session | 21 | 14 | 1 | 30 |
| In-Person Proofing — American Job Center | 30 | 14 | 1 | 30 |
| In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location | 30 | 14 | 1 | 30 |
| Documentary Verification by Mail | 30 | 21 | 1 | 30 |
| Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification | 45 | 21 | 2 | 60 |

## Schedule B — Notice, timeliness and mail review

| Pathway | Notice channel | Date that decides whether documents met the deadline | Mail review after receipt (business days) | Does a pathway change restart the deadline? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Online Identity Proofing (IAL2) | email and postal mail | date received | 0 | no |
| Video Trusted Referee Session | email and postal mail | date received | 0 | no |
| In-Person Proofing — American Job Center | email and postal mail | date received | 0 | no |
| In-Person Proofing — USPS Retail Location | email and postal mail | date received | 0 | no |
| Documentary Verification by Mail | email and postal mail | postmark date | 10 | no |
| Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification | email and postal mail | postmark date | 10 | no |

## Notes to the schedules

1. The deadline column is the number of calendar days after the date of the identity verification notice by which verification must be completed.
2. The extension column is the number of calendar days one approved extension adds to the verification deadline; the next column is how many such extensions one case may receive.
3. The late completion column is the number of calendar days after the verification deadline within which an expired case may be reopened with good cause.
4. A mail review period of 0 business days means documents are not mailed on that pathway; where documents are mailed, the agency takes the listed number of business days to review them after receipt.
5. On every pathway the identity verification notice is sent by both email and postal mail, and on no pathway does a change of pathway restart the deadline.

## Figures worked from the schedule

- On Identity Theft Victim Re-Verification, the two extensions allowed, each of 21 days, can add 42 calendar days in total to the deadline.
- On every other pathway one extension is allowed, so the most that extensions can add is 14 days (online, video, American Job Center, USPS retail office) or 21 days (mail).
- Only the two pathways whose timeliness date is the postmark (mail and identity theft re-verification) have a mail review period other than 0.
